outcome: Successful TOLAC (Vaginal Birth After Cesarean - VBAC)
maternal outcomes (symptomatic uterine rupture, hysterectomy, maternal death)
cohort: Women with one prior cesarean delivery who delivered in a tertiary medical center between 2008 and 2019.
finding: The study reported an 81.92% VBAC success rate, found uterine rupture to be rare and not associated with severe adverse outcomes, and developed a decision-tree algorithm identifying maternal age, gestational age at delivery, and history of vaginal delivery as key predictors for successful TOLAC.
mod_finding: The rate of successful TOLAC (VBAC) was 81.92%, with symptomatic uterine rupture occurring in 0.98% of women and not associated with severe maternal or neonatal morbidity or mortality; women with a prior vaginal delivery had the highest likelihood of VBAC (90.3%).
gest_age: Gestational age at delivery was measured and identified as a predictor for VBAC success.
